data.name: Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls
data.detailed_description:
Komaru Naegi, little sister to Makoto Naegi, has been imprisoned inside a mysterious apartment for over a year. One day, she is rescued by Byakuya Togami of Future Foundation, but the rescue is derailed by a sudden attack of hundreds of Monokumas. Komaru soon discovers that the city has been taken over by a group of children calling themselves the Warriors of Hope. Their leader, Monaca, declares that the city will be the site of a “children's paradise,” and to accomplish this, all the adults will be exterminated. Komaru teams up with Toko Fukawa to try to survive the rampaging Monokumas, escape the crafty Monokuma Kids, and uncover the secrets of the city.

Key Features
  • Third Person Shooter Action Sequences: Use Future Foundation's Hacking Gun to have a fighting chance against the hordes of Monokumasas you traverse Towa City.
  • Riddles and Puzzles: The MonokumaKids will challenge more than just your trigger finger; you'll need your smarts to survive as well. There's a lot to discover in the city, with a number of familiar faces and mysteries to unravel!
  • Tons of Different Types of Ammo: Tackle challenges with multiple kinds of Truth Bullets, such as Paralyze and Link. Upgrade your firepower with special Bling Bullet modifiers.
  • Steam Features: Supports Steam Achievements, Steam Cloud and Steam Trading Cards

reviews.review:
This game isn't good, but my goodness is it something.

As someone who only just recently got into DanganRonpa and enjoyed the first 2 games a fair bit, i heard literal horror stories about this game, some even claiming it is one of the worst games ever made.
While i can see why someone would feel that way, for me this game is kinda fascinating and i can't help but kind of admire it for how much it sticks to it's guns. Ultra Despair Girls carries the same vibe as an obscure horror game from the PS2 whose sole purpose was to polarize the audience with its themes and sole existence.

I usually do not like seperating game and experience into two different descriptions for a game at all, but i think it really is necessary for this one.
Mainly because for the "game portion", Ultra Despair Girls isn't particularly special. It is a below average third person shooter with some alright puzzles thrown in. Good ideas but it never goes anywhere beyond that really. Genocide Jacks Gameplay is equally as basic.
Even on the highest difficulty it never is by any means hard or challenging either. Even so it managed to get a good horror game vibe going from time to time.

However i want to talk specifically about the experience itself. The presentation is one of the best i have seen in a long time in a videogame, the last time it was arguably a Persona game. From the cute menus, the weird UI, the colorful graphics and locals, the sound design and especially the music; it truly is second to none in terms of stylish and unique.
Unapologetically strange i would call it. It is where this game shines so good it makes it impossible for me to hate.

And then there's the story and writing. I think many valid things have already been said about it, but that a silly game like this would tackle the topic cycle of abuse in the way it is oddly..... fascinating to me.
Like i can't tell if this game is deliberate in making the player highly uncomfortable as much as possible or if it is legit just so tone deaf and is missing the hypocrisy by accident. Many times you don't fully know what the game WANTS to tell you and it never really provides a full explaination.

I think especially Chapter 3 will be the breaking point to most people on where they will stop playing or dredge through the rest. The game by that point also really dips in quality, chapter 4 and 5 being just kind of bad in their own right. The ending was sweet though.

Komaru and Toko absolutely steal the show. They are both very cute protagonists and i got so many good laughs out of Toko especially. It's really sweet how these two get closer and braver throughout the journey, like Komaru starts to not be as shaky in her model later on, it's good stuff. They also just bounce of well off each other.
It can get rather repetetive though hearing Komaru be sad on how shes weak and ordinary over and over again. Almost feel like they didn't really knew how to advance her arc - horror game heroine syndrome and what not.

The rest of the cast is sadly fairly weak. Haiji has to be the worst character in the series and the Warriors of Hope i wish would have gotten a bit more development and better treatment by the writing.

I feel like by the moment the game was made they planned it to be highly polarizing. A game about child abuse and that trauma manifested in a world brought to the end by robot bears is a highly unserious idea..... but where ELSE would you get this kind of stuff?

I doubt i will play anything like this in a long time and i do not want this game to be anything else than it currently is.
You aren't a good game Ultra Despair Girls and i certainly can not recommend you to anybody, but you sure left an impact. 

And to me, that is more admirable than a safe, great game ever could be.
